imam.docTitle: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS) | Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim
imam.description: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS): his birth and lineage, titles, character, knowledge and worship, his role in preserving the teachings of Islam, and his standing among Muslims.
imam.title: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
imam.lede: The seventh Imam of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS). Born at al-Abwa, he died a martyr in the Abbasid prisons of Baghdad after an imamate of thirty-five years, known throughout as the one of long prostrations and the Gate of Needs to God.

martyrdom.label: Martyrdom
martyrdom.note: In the prison of al-Sindi ibn Shahik, Baghdad

imam.branchesTitle: The Imam's life in six chapters

wilada.title: Birth and Lineage
wilada.body:
Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) was born at al-Abwa, a halt between Mecca and Medina, on 7 Safar 128 AH according to the best-known account. His father, Imam al-Sadiq (AS), was returning from the Hajj and greeted his birth with joy.

His father was Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (AS), the sixth Imam of the Ahl al-Bayt, and his mother was Lady Hamida the Purified, of whom Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said: “Hamida is purified of all impurity, like an ingot of gold.”
wilada.lineage: Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them)
wilada.kunya: He was known as Abu al-Hasan and Abu Ibrahim.

alqab.title: His Titles
alqab.intro: Each of his titles tells a story that bears witness to one of his qualities:

kadhim.name: Al-Kadhim
kadhim.why: “The one who restrains his anger”: he swallowed his anger and answered harm with kindness, until the title eclipsed his name.

salih.name: The Righteous Servant
salih.why: A title by which narrators knew him, for his abundant worship and long prostrations.

hawaij.name: The Gate of Needs
hawaij.why: Because people found their needs fulfilled when they sought his intercession with God Almighty.

sabir.name: The Patient, the Trustworthy
sabir.why: For his patience through trial and imprisonment, and his faithfulness to the religion of his grandfather, the Messenger of God (PBUH).

akhlaq.title: His Character
akhlaq.body:
He answered harm with kindness. It is narrated that a man of Medina used to insult him and speak ill of the Commander of the Faithful (AS). Some of his companions wanted to strike the man, but he forbade them. Instead he visited the man at his farm, treated him generously and gave him money, until the man's heart changed and he began to say: “God knows best where to place His message.”

By night he looked after the poor of Medina, carrying purses of dinars to them while they never knew where the gifts came from, until people made a proverb of “the purses of Musa”.

ilm.title: Knowledge and Worship
ilm.sujud: He was known for prostrations so long that he was called “the companion of the long prostration”. Among his supplications in prostration:
ilm.dua: “Great is the sin of Your servant; so let the pardon from You be beautiful.”
ilm.prison: When he was imprisoned he said: “O God, I used to ask You to free me for Your worship. O God, You have done so; to You belongs all praise.” He turned his cell into a place of prayer.
ilm.knowledge: He was the reference of his age in knowledge. His companions, and those of his father, narrated a great deal of hadith and jurisprudence from him, and among the most precious of his teachings is his counsel to Hisham ibn al-Hakam on reason and wisdom.

hifz.title: His Role in Preserving the Teachings of Islam
hifz.context: He assumed the imamate in 148 AH after his father's martyrdom, in the reign of the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur, and lived on under al-Mahdi, al-Hadi and Harun al-Rashid, while the authorities watched the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) and their followers and pressed hard upon them.
hifz.deed1: He preserved the school of his father Imam al-Sadiq (AS), passing jurisprudence, hadith and doctrine on to his companions.
hifz.deed2: He built a network of representatives across the lands, linking people to their Imam and carrying his answers back to them.
hifz.deed3: He refused to lend legitimacy to the oppressor: he reproached Safwan the camel-hirer for renting his camels to Harun, even for the road to Hajj, to teach his companions not to incline toward those who do wrong.

makana.title: His Standing among Muslims
makana.body: Muslims agree on his knowledge, his worship and his generosity. His shrine in Kadhimiya, Baghdad, beside his grandson Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS), draws pilgrims from every corner of the world, and millions walk to it each year on the anniversary of his martyrdom.
makana.quote: “Whenever a matter troubled me and I went to the grave of Musa ibn Ja'far and sought intercession through him, God made easy for me what I wished.”
makana.quoteSource: Abu Ali al-Khallal, the leading Hanbali scholar of his time, as narrated by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in Tarikh Baghdad

sira.docTitle: Life, Oppression and Martyrdom of the Imam | Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim
sira.description: The circumstances of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), his prisons from Basra to Baghdad, the accounts of his martyrdom in 183 AH, and the meanings of patience and steadfastness in his memory.
sira.title: Life, Oppression and Martyrdom
sira.lede: Thirty-five years of imamate, the last of them spent between shackles and dungeons; yet prison only drew him nearer to his Lord.

circumstances.caption: Steadfast in chains
circumstances.alt: Artistic depiction of the Imam (AS) bound in chains, raising his finger to the sky, his face bathed in light
circumstances.title: The Times He Lived In
circumstances.body:
Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) assumed the imamate in 148 AH after the martyrdom of his father Imam al-Sadiq (AS), with the Abbasid state at the height of its tyranny. Al-Mansur had resolved to kill whomever Imam al-Sadiq named as his successor, so the Imam (AS) named five people in his will, the first of them al-Mansur himself, to protect his son from being killed.

He then lived under al-Mahdi, who had him brought to Baghdad and later released, and under al-Hadi after him, until Harun al-Rashid came to power. The persecution of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) and their followers intensified; the Imam watched his companions hunted and imprisoned, while he remained patient, preserving the religion of his grandfather and strengthening the patience of his followers.

prison.caption: A prayer in the dungeon
prison.alt: Artistic depiction of a kneeling prisoner raising his palms in prayer, chains on his wrists, in the darkness of a dungeon
prison.title: Imprisonment, from Medina to Baghdad
prison.intro: In 179 AH Harun ordered the Imam's arrest. He was seized while standing in prayer at the grave of his grandfather, the Messenger of God (PBUH), and a long journey through prisons began, each link harsher than the one before:

medina.note: Arrested in his grandfather's mosque and carried off in chains.

basra.place: Basra: the prison of Isa ibn Ja'far
basra.note: About a year, until Isa, moved by the Imam's worship, wrote to Harun asking to be relieved of him.

rabi.place: Baghdad: the prison of al-Fadl ibn al-Rabi'
rabi.note: Moved to the capital of the caliphate, where his imprisonment grew long.

yahya.place: Baghdad: the prison of al-Fadl ibn Yahya
yahya.note: He eased the Imam's confinement and was punished for it.

sindi.place: Baghdad: the prison of al-Sindi ibn Shahik
sindi.note: The harshest and cruelest of the prisons, where his martyrdom came.

prison.outro: In the darkness of the dungeons the Imam neither complained nor compromised. He spent his nights and days in prostration, until his jailers were overwhelmed by his worship, and he said: “O God, I used to ask You to free me for Your worship. O God, You have done so; to You belongs all praise.”

martyrdom.caption: The green turban
martyrdom.alt: A green turban stained with blood, resting on a stone, symbolizing the martyrdom of the Imam (AS)
martyrdom.title: Accounts of His Martyrdom
martyrdom.body:
In the prison of al-Sindi ibn Shahik he was poisoned on Harun's orders, and he died a martyr on 25 Rajab 183 AH according to the best-known account, at the age of fifty-five.

Wanting to clear the authorities of blame, al-Sindi brought a group of Baghdad's notables to the Imam so they would testify that he had come to no harm; but the Imam (AS) told them that he had been poisoned.

His pure body was then laid on the bridge of Baghdad and a call meant to belittle him was proclaimed over it, until Sulayman ibn Abi Ja'far came out, took up the body and shrouded it. The people carried him in procession to the Quraysh cemetery, where his shrine stands today in Holy Kadhimiya.

meaning.caption: Patience and steadfastness
meaning.title: What the Anniversary Means
meaning.intro: Prison did not break the Imam; it revealed his true metal: patience that never complains, prostration that no shackle can interrupt, and steadfastness in the truth that never bargains. That is why the day of his martyrdom became a time to renew the covenant.

patience.name: Patience
patience.text: That the heart remain content with God's decree, however narrow the walls.

steadfastness.name: Steadfastness
steadfastness.text: That the oppressor be given no legitimacy, even at the cost of a whole life.

loyalty.name: Loyalty
loyalty.text: That the memory be revived every year: pilgrims walk to Kadhimiya, and gatherings are held in homes and associations.

nasab.docTitle: The Imam's Family and Lineage | Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim
nasab.description: The father of Imam al-Kadhim (AS), Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq; his mother, Lady Hamida; his children and household; and his noble lineage reaching Imam al-Husayn and Imam Ali (AS), down to the sayyids, the sons of Sayyid Nasir.
nasab.title: The Imam's Family and Lineage
nasab.lede: A lineage whose links are never broken: from the Commander of the Faithful (AS) to Imam al-Kadhim (AS), and from him to the descendants who carry his name today.

father.name: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (AS)
father.text: The sixth Imam of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) and head of the greatest school of learning of his age, where thousands of narrators and scholars studied; the Ja'fari school bears his name. From him Imam al-Kadhim (AS) received knowledge and the imamate.

mother.name: Lady Hamida the Purified
mother.text: She was known for her knowledge, piety and chastity, and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) praised her. Among his words about her:
mother.quote: “Hamida is purified of all impurity, like an ingot of gold.”

lineage.title: The Noble Lineage
lineage.intro: Hashimite, Alawite, Husaynite; from his descendants come the Musawi sayyids, among them the sons of Sayyid Nasir.

kadhim.name: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS)

mujab.name: Sayyid Ibrahim al-Mujab
mujab.role: Buried in the Husayni shrine in Karbala

sons.name: Sons of Sayyid Nasir
sons.role: Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) Association, Holy Najaf

mujab.title: Sayyid Ibrahim al-Mujab
mujab.body:
He is Ibrahim, son of Muhammad al-Abid, son of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS). He is said to have been the first of the Alawites to settle beside the shrine of Imam al-Husayn, and his tomb lies today within the Husayni shrine in holy Karbala.

He was called “al-Mujab”, the one who was answered, because he stood at the grave of his forefather al-Husayn (AS) and said: “Peace be upon you, O father,” and an answer was heard from the grave: “And upon you be peace, O my son.”

From his descendants the Musawi sayyids spread across Iraq, among them the sons of Sayyid Nasir, who founded this association.

children.title: His Children and Household
children.intro: Sheikh al-Mufid records that Imam al-Kadhim (AS) had thirty-seven children, sons and daughters, whose descendants spread across many lands. Among the most renowned:

rida.name: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS)
rida.text: The eighth Imam of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS); his shrine is in Mashhad.

masuma.name: Lady Fatima al-Ma'suma (SA)
masuma.text: The noble lady of the Ahl al-Bayt; her shrine is in Qom.

ahmad.name: Sayyid Ahmad ibn Musa
ahmad.text: Known as Shah Cheragh; his shrine is in Shiraz.

muhammad.name: Sayyid Muhammad ibn Musa al-Abid
muhammad.text: Called al-Abid, “the worshipper”, for his abundant prayer and devotion; his shrine is in Shiraz, and the sons of Sayyid Nasir descend from him.

hayaa.docTitle: Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) | Holy Najaf, al-Iskan Quarter
hayaa.description: The Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) Association: why it was founded, when it began, its founders the sons of Sayyid Nasir, its mission, and the mourning gatherings it holds.
hayaa.title: Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim (AS)
hayaa.lede: A Husseini association in the al-Iskan quarter of Holy Najaf, led by the sons of Sayyid Nasir.

who.title: Who we are
who.statement: We are Hashimite, Alawite, Husaynite and Musawi sayyids. Our lineage reaches Sayyid Ibrahim al-Mujab, son of Sayyid Muhammad al-Abid, son of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (AS); we are his descendants, and from this the association takes its name.

founding.title: Why We Began
founding.p1: This association was not born from nothing. The gathering we hold today is an old one, kept alive by our fathers and grandfathers since long ago. Year after year they lit within it the lamp of grief for the tragedy of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), with whatever means they had and with hearts that never tired.
founding.p2: That is how we were raised: grief for al-Husayn and his family (AS) is a covenant that never lapses, and being a sayyid is not a lineage to be recited but a character to be lived.
founding.p3: These are the qualities of our forefathers from the family of Muhammad (PBUH), foremost among them our grandfather Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS), who was named al-Kadhim because he restrained his anger.
founding.p4: So that this gathering may endure after us as it endured after our fathers, the sons of Sayyid Nasir came together to give this legacy the form of an association bearing their grandfather's name.

past.when: Since the days of our forefathers
past.what: An old mourning gathering, held in the homes of the sayyids and handed down from parents to children.
past.alt: An old photograph of the sayyids in our fathers' days, sitting together around a large pot of food

now.what: The Descendants of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) Association begins its work in the al-Iskan quarter of Holy Najaf.
now.alt: The sayyids, sons of Sayyid Nasir, gathered with their children in their majlis today

founders.label: The Founders
founders.name: Sons of Sayyid Nasir
founders.text: The sons and grandsons of Sayyid Nasir, Musawi sayyids, who carried on their fathers' gathering and built this association upon it, in service of their grandfather Imam al-Kadhim (AS) and the Ahl al-Bayt (AS).

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.statement: To keep the voice of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) alive within us: patience in the face of injustice, prostration that no shackle can interrupt, and generosity that walks by night without a name. We hold mourning gatherings in loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt (AS), raise our children in them as we were raised, and open our doors to every lover, servant and visitor.

revival.name: Revival
revival.text: Holding mourning gatherings in their seasons, and keeping the memory of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) alive in homes and hearts.

loyalty.name: Loyalty
loyalty.text: Preserving the legacy of our forefathers and passing the gathering on to our children as it reached us.

service.name: Service
service.text: Welcoming and serving the mourners, and following the way of the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) in generosity and restraint of anger.

majalis.title: Our Gatherings
majalis.intro: The mourning occasions the association observes every year:

kadhim.title: Anniversary of the Martyrdom of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS)
kadhim.text: A mourning gathering recalling the Imam's suffering in the prisons of Baghdad, and his patience and steadfastness unto martyrdom.

ashura.title: The First Ten Days of Sacred Muharram
ashura.text: Reviving the ten nights of Ashura with recitation and Husseini mourning gatherings, through to the night of the tenth.

night.title: A Mourning Gathering on One Night of Sacred Muharram
night.text: An annual gathering the association holds on one night of the month of grief, in loyalty to the Master of Martyrs (AS).
